why: The OTHER way to get the counter-rotation wrong, and the reason the derivation is written out in the function's own comment. A flipped sign does not hold the marker still and does not leave it alone: it spins it at DOUBLE rate. At small turn rates that reads as wobble rather than as a bug, which is exactly how a wrong sign survives a look-at-it review. Filed separately from the returns-zero entry above because the two are different mistakes with different symptoms, and an assertion that caught only one of them would leave the likelier one uncovered.
